sources.entry: Realign - Saves a window layout per display setup and puts every window back with one shortcut, or automatically when you dock or undock.

summary.one_liner: Realign is a macOS menu bar app that saves window layouts per display setup and restores them via keyboard shortcut or automatically when monitors are connected or disconnected.
summary.what_it_does: Realign saves the current positions and sizes of your Mac windows as a layout. It keeps one saved layout for the laptop alone and one for each set of external monitors, and saving again overwrites the layout for the current display setup. A keyboard shortcut (Ctrl+Option+Cmd+R by default) restores the layout matching the connected displays, and Ctrl+Option+Cmd+S saves the current layout. Menu options let you restore the laptop or multi-display layout directly, change what the shortcut restores, and turn on auto-restore when a monitor is plugged in or unplugged (off by default). It needs macOS Accessibility permission to move windows.
use_cases: Restore window positions after plugging in external monitors
Automatically rearrange windows when docking or undocking a laptop
Save and recall a preferred window layout with a keyboard shortcut
Keep separate window arrangements for laptop-only and multi-monitor setups
Reset scattered windows back to a known layout on macOS
how_to_run: Or download the zip from the latest release and drag Realign to your Applications folder
git clone <repository URL> (the README leaves the URL blank)
On first launch, grant Accessibility access when macOS asks
notable: Separate saved layouts for laptop-only and each external-monitor setup
Auto-restore triggered when monitors are plugged in or unplugged
Configurable shortcut target: matching layout, laptop layout, or multi-display layout
caveats: Needs Accessibility access granted on first launch to move windows
